title: BINUH/OHCHR Report: 613 Killed in Plaine du Cul-de-Sac and Cité Soleil Since March
detail: The UN's political office in Haiti (BINUH) and Designated Human Rights Expert William O'Neill published a report on August 6, 2026 documenting 613 people killed and 375 injured between March 6 and July 31, 2026 in just two Port-au-Prince neighborhoods — Plaine du Cul-de-Sac and Cité Soleil. Over one-third of victims were not gang-affiliated, including 111 women and 77 children; 176 women and girls were raped by gang members, and 18,000+ people were displaced. The report documents specific atrocities including the execution of two 17-year-old boys on suspicion of gang affiliation, a 71-year-old man killed while requesting food, a woman executed after being unable to answer a gang's questioning, 17 boys aged 15-17 executed together at a trash site, and the June 13 massacre of 61 people (including seven children) celebrating Haiti's World Cup qualification match. O'Neill described the violence as 'wanton, intentional infliction of incredible pain,' with victims frequently caught merely in the wrong place at the wrong time.

media.caption: UN details atrocities by gangs in Haiti's Plaine du Cul-de-Sac and Cité Soleil

title: PNH Divisional Inspector Waldeck Valcourt Kidnapped in Delmas 31
detail: Haitian National Police (PNH) Divisional Inspector Waldeck Valcourt was kidnapped in the Delmas 31 area of Port-au-Prince on August 6, 2026, the latest in a string of high-profile abductions of officials that also included Ecclésiaste Télémaque, chief of staff to the education minister, abducted in the same area on July 24, and James Boyard, chief of staff to the defense minister, abducted June 11 and still held captive as of the report. Civil society figures including Pierre Espérance publicly alleged police involvement in kidnapping networks, saying 'the country's highest authorities know this.'

media.caption: Gangs ramp up attacks and kidnappings in Haiti as election security concerns grow

title: Sri Lankan GSF Contingent Lands in Gonaïves, Artibonite
detail: Sri Lankan Gang Suppression Force (GSF) soldiers arrived by ship at the port of Gonaïves, Artibonite department, on August 6, 2026, with vehicles, tactical equipment, and heavy machinery — the first GSF contingent deployment outside the Port-au-Prince metro area since the force's June 1 full-operations launch. The deployment is intended to support the Haitian National Police (PNH) against armed groups in Artibonite, the country's second-most affected department (381 killed in 2026 year-to-date, 25.7% of the national total), where Gran Grif and Kokorat San Ras gangs have expanded largely unchecked along Route Nationale corridors.
